definition: Gender assignment is the process of linking a noun to a grammatical gender category such as masculine, feminine, or neuter. In the context of compound-word recognition, the packet supports that this assignment is mainly guided by the compound’s head rather than by the embedded modifier.

reasons: The packet does not explicitly define “gender assignment” as a general process of linking a noun to grammatical gender (masculine/feminine/neuter). It only discusses grammatical gender in the context of determiner primes and noun-noun compound recognition.

Although the claim that, in compound-word recognition, gender is mainly guided by the compound’s head rather than the modifier is supported (“Head-congruent determiner primes speeded compound recognition… no effects… for modifier-congruent primes” and “head-driven gender assignment”).

The opening general definition is broader than what the packet supports; the source only shows head-driven grammatical gender assignment during German noun-noun compound recognition, not a general process of linking any noun to a grammatical gender category.
The definition mixes a general lexicographic sense with a study-specific experimental finding; the packet supports only the compound-recognition context and the head-vs-modifier effect.
